english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{12}+y^{2}=1$ and let $H$ be the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{8}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}=1$. For $\lambda>0$, let $P$ be the pole of the line $x+y=\lambda$ with respect to $E$ and let $Q$ be the pole of the same line with respect to $H$. If $PQ=4$, then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{12}+y^{2}=1$ है तथा $H$ अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{x^{2}}{8}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}=1$ है। $\lambda>0$ के लिए, माना कि $E$ के सापेक्ष रेखा $x+y=\lambda$ का ध्रुव $P$ है तथा $H$ के सापेक्ष इसी रेखा का ध्रुव $Q$ है। यदि $PQ=4$ है, तो $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The polar of a point $(h,k)$ with respect to $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ is $\dfrac{hx}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{ky}{b^{2}}=1$, and with respect to $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ it is $\dfrac{hx}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{ky}{b^{2}}=1$. The pole of a line is the point whose polar is that line.
Pole with respect to $E$: $\dfrac{h}{12}=\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$ and $k=\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$, so $P=\left(\dfrac{12}{\lambda},\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\right)$.
Pole with respect to $H$: $\dfrac{h}{8}=\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$ and $-\dfrac{k}{2}=\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$, so $Q=\left(\dfrac{8}{\lambda},-\dfrac{2}{\lambda}\right)$.

concept_use.Pole and polar for Hyperbola: Q is found by matching the polar hx/8 - ky/2 = 1 with x + y = lambda, giving Q(8/lambda, -2/lambda).
concept_use.Pole and polar for Ellipse: P is found by matching the polar hx/12 + ky = 1 with x + y = lambda, giving P(12/lambda, 1/lambda).

originality_note: New: the same line is given poles with respect to an ellipse and a hyperbola; their separation scales as 1/lambda and fixes the line (way 5). Closest known: pole of a given line with respect to an ellipse. Different because: two poles of one line with respect to two different conics are compared, and the distance between them, not either pole, is the condition.
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter introduced, conditions complete (quadrant / sign / branch stated), one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer equals the plan (positive decimal: 1.25). Changed: No change. Checked that lambda > 0 makes the answer unique and that the line does not pass through the common centre, so both poles exist.
key_step: Match the polar forms of E and H with x/lambda + y/lambda = 1 to get both poles, then use the distance.
justification: Routine chain of standard steps (two pole computations and a distance) with no insight. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q4 (L2), a routine ellipse tangent/chord computation.
